acceptance_rule: Correctness, originality, and value must all pass.

correctness.rationale: The unrestricted upper bound is Madrid's exact norm. The lower construction was independently reconstructed: the finite product martingale has maximal-to-terminal ratio tending to \(p'\); unbounded logarithmic diameter supplies arbitrarily long multiplicatively separated finite radius chains; the base-\(B\) digit model freezes past coordinates and averages future coordinates with explicit boundary error; periodic localization and \(L^p\)-stable smoothing preserve the ratio. Numerical checks of the martingale constant \((1-q)/(1-q^{1/p'})\) for large \(B\) converge to \(p'\) for several \(p\).
residual_risks: Madrid's full preprint remained inaccessible, so only its exact unrestricted theorem from the primary abstract was used.

evidence: A public review reports a dyadic special case in Madrid's work; that case is conservatively treated as prior coverage.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A single geometric sequence does not dominate all arbitrary irregular sets.

evidence: Those prior results give the upper bound and special radius families but not the prescribed-scale martingale realization for every escaping set.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The finite-subfamily near-extremizer theorem is the additional nontrivial implication.
searches: Madrid unrestricted norm plus Wei truncation versus arbitrary thinning

evidence: No earlier exact arbitrary-radius theorem was located; the known continuous truncation is not equivalent.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A full interval of radii is much richer than an arbitrary escaping sparse set, so the 2016 truncation theorem does not imply the final claim.
searches: centered maximal prescribed radii exact norm

evidence: The assigned record was the only exact semantic hit.

originality.rationale: Wei–Nie–Wu–Yan prove equality for the continuous truncation \(0<r<\gamma\), and Madrid's current work gives the unrestricted exact norm; the assigned result is stronger in a different direction, allowing arbitrary irregular or superlacunary prescribed sets with only scale escape. Resultary returned no earlier arbitrary-radius theorem.
residual_risks: Madrid's full text was not obtained; if it contains a theorem for arbitrary prescribed radius sets, originality would need revision. This inaccessible plausible source alone was not taken as a failure under the stated audit rule.

source_inspections.material_read: open-access full article, including abstract/definitions and norm-equality theorem

source_inspections.assessment: Establishes unrestricted exact norm; plausible residual broader-coverage risk.
source_inspections.material_read: primary abstract; full text retrieval failed through direct open routes and institutional retrieval returned no verified PDF

value.rationale: The theorem shows a sharp rigidity phenomenon under arbitrarily severe scale thinning and gives finite prescribed-scale near-extremizers. That is a natural structural strengthening of a newly solved sharp-norm problem and is not an arbitrary finite slice.
residual_risks: The result is one-dimensional and leaves radius sets in a compact annulus and endpoint/higher-dimensional questions open.

final_claim: For every nonempty set of radii \(\mathcal R\subset(0,\infty)\) with unbounded logarithmic diameter and every \(1<p<\infty\), the one-dimensional centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator restricted to \(\mathcal R\) has exact \(L^p\) norm \(p'=p/(p-1)\); finite subsets of \(\mathcal R\) already admit smooth compactly supported near-extremizers.
